tagline: A seven-mile loop of farm lanes, beach and the bishop's rock.
intro: The loop runs about seven miles around the southeast corner of Middletown on Aquidneck Island, on narrow roads between canopy trees, stone walls and fields on some of the most fertile soil in Rhode Island. Taken counterclockwise, Berkeley Avenue becomes Paradise Avenue and runs south through a tunnel of trees beside the Maidford River, down to the shore.

Past Second Beach the road slips beneath the face of Hanging Rock into the woods and comes out on Indian Avenue, among Shingle-style houses with views down to the Sakonnet River. Then it turns west through farm and nursery country on Peckham, Wapping and Wyatt.

moments.title: Whitehall
moments.text: Finely crafted stone walls mark the way in to Whitehall, the farmhouse George Berkeley bought in 1729 and enlarged to his own design while he worked toward a college he planned for Bermuda.

moments.title: Second Beach
moments.text: Where Paradise Avenue meets Hanging Rock Road the view opens south over Narragansett Bay to the Purgatory Chasm bluffs, with St. George's Gothic chapel up on its hill.

moments.title: Hanging Rock
moments.text: A trail from the Norman Bird Sanctuary climbs the rock that Bishop Berkeley made a favorite haunt, and its view of beaches, ocean and reservoir turns up in several paintings by LaFarge.

sources.label: Town of Middletown and RI Scenic Highways Board, The Paradise Loop Scenic Highway Stewardship Plan
